hypotheses.note: conjugue W (Prop. 3 2°); under (b) or (c) closes with no Lean change; under (a) the statement of record is with « the conjugate meeting L only at 0 » (conjugue_eq_of_disjoint) or « the least distinguished conjugate » (conjugue_le_of_sontConjugues)

findings: No proof is printed (l.524 « De là on déduit aussitôt le »). The derivation is not immediate from Théorème 1 alone: it uses that the projection P_L along the conjugate preserves every distinguished subspace (Théorème 1's proof step, projection_mem_of_mem) three times — for closure under ∩ (conjugate L' + D', De Morgan), under + (conjugate L' ∩ D') and for distributivity.

« comme sup le produit » (l.531; so printed in the scan, journal p. 267) means the sum L + D: once inf is ∩ the order is inclusion and the sup is forced to be L ⊔ D, which is distinguished (estDistingue_sup).
questions: OQ-163 (Déf. 4) and « on prend comme complémentaire le conjugué »: the complement is Prop. 3 2°'s unique supplementary conjugate (conjugue W L). Under (b) it is the conjugate; under (c) the only distinguished conjugate (conjugue_eq_of_isSommeConvexes); under (a) (no supplementarity) it is the least distinguished conjugate and the only conjugate meeting L at 0 (conjugue_le_of_sontConjugues, conjugue_eq_of_disjoint), but not every (a)-conjugate is the complement: ℝ is (a)-conjugate to itself relative to [0,∞[, while its complement is 0 (demiDroite_complement_conjugue). The row is left unmarked (AUDIT-1) until OQ-163 is ruled: under (b) or (c) it closes with no Lean change; under (a) the statement of record is with « the conjugate meeting L only at 0 » or « the least distinguished conjugate ».

labels.label: bzcor:c3s2t2c_algebre_parties_affine

hypotheses.paper: E de dimension finie n (and Théorème 2's W)
hypotheses.note: FiniteDimensional ℝ E, n = Module.finrank ℝ E; W's four hypotheses
the lower bound is carried under 0 < n only; false at n = 0

findings: « imprecise » (l.537–538): « le cardinal est compris entre 1 et n » fails at n = 0. For E = 0 (e.g. W = [−1,1]⁰) the hypotheses of Théorème 2 hold, there is exactly one distinguished subspace (0 = E) and no simple one, so the Boolean algebra is the algebra of parts of the empty set (cardinal 0), and is not order-isomorphic to the parts of any nonempty set (cube_zero_corollaire, simples_eq_empty_of_finrank_eq_zero). Proved corrected form: card ≤ n always, card ≥ 1 when n ≥ 1 (corollaire_algebre_parties). Compare OQ-45 (a).

Everything else is proved as printed: the simple distinguished subspaces form a finite set S with |S| ≤ n, T ↦ ∑ T is an order isomorphism Set S ≃o {distinguished subspaces} (isoParties), and every distinguished subspace is the sum of exactly one set of simple ones. The extremes are attained: the cube [−1,1]ⁿ has exactly the n coordinate axes as simple subspaces (cube_simples, cube_simples_ncard), the closed unit ball of a nonzero Euclidean space has the single simple subspace E (boule_simples_ncard).
questions: « l'algèbre des parties d'un ensemble fini » is formalized as an order isomorphism with Set (simples W) (an order isomorphism of Boolean algebras preserves all Boolean operations); « famille » is read as a set of simple subspaces (no repetition — the uniqueness needs it).

« 1 correspond à la sphère » is read as the closed unit ball (the convex body bounded by the sphere) and as an example only, not as « cardinal 1 iff W is a ball » (cardinal 1 means only that W has no nontrivial decomposition; the converse is not claimed here, nor formalized).
Is the degenerate case E = 0 (n = 0) implicitly excluded by « dimension finie n »? If so the printed statement is the formalized one with 0 < n, and the row could be marked under that ruling.

OQ-163: the Corollary speaks of Théorème 2's Boolean algebra, whose complement is « le conjugué »; the isomorphism isoParties is an order isomorphism and does not depend on the reading, but the row inherits Théorème 2's OQ-163 dependence.

instances: cube [−1,1]ⁿ: cube_hyps (Fibres) gives the hypotheses; cube_algebreBoole : BooleanAlgebra (Distingues (cube n)); cube_isoParties : Set (simples (cube n)) ≃o Distingues (cube n); cube_simples, cube_simples_ncard = n; cube_estSimple_coord (an EstSimple term)
closed unit ball of a real inner product space: boule_hyps (convex, 0, spanning, no line), boule_simples = {⊤}, boule_simples_ncard = 1 (Nontrivial E)
kb_proposals: Chapter3/BooleAffine: the distinguished subspaces are closed under ⊓ and ⊔ with conjugue (L ⊓ D) = conjugue L ⊔ conjugue D and conjugue (L ⊔ D) = conjugue L ⊓ conjugue D (estDistingue_inf/sup, conjugue_inf/sup); the Boolean algebra is algebreBoole on Distingues W, whose order is the Subtype order (so Subtype lemmas apply); Théorème 3 (projective) should transfer through it.

Chapter3/BooleAffine: for finite-dimensional counting arguments on distinguished subspaces use simples W, isoParties, le_sSup_iff_mem_of_estSimple (a simple subspace below a finite sum of simple ones is one of them) and ncard_le_finrank_sSup; a minimal element by finrank is obtained with (measure finrank).wf.has_min.

Building a BooleanAlgebra on a subtype of a non-distributive lattice: Subtype.lattice + DistribLattice.ofInfSupLe + Subtype.boundedOrder, then a structure instance with compl, inf_compl_le_bot, top_le_sup_compl; mark the def @[implicit_reducible] (a class-valued def warns otherwise at this pin).
